researchAgentWebSearchValidation.rootCause: Level B, precisely isolated: native function-calling tool injection (search_web/fetch_url) in the real, installed OpenWebUI 0.11.1 source is gated on a non-empty metadata.session_id (utils/middleware.py's use_builtin_tools) -- a plain Bearer-token API call without one never receives the tool at all. With session_id present, tool injection and the model's own tool-calling behavior are both correct. OpenWebUI's own further automatic background-task execution/continuation of that tool call (used when session_id and a real chat_id are both present) has a separate, real, reproducible stall after the initial knowledge_search preprocessing step, independent of Redis/SearXNG availability -- an OpenWebUI-core limitation for non-browser callers, not an Agent Pack or model defect, and out of scope to patch from this repository.
researchAgentWebSearchValidation.change: No Agent Pack code change was required -- ki-stack-research's own provisioned fields (capabilities.web_search, builtinTools.web_search, params.function_calling=native, real Knowledge binding) were already correct, confirmed by reading the live OpenWebUI object back directly.

targetSystemMutationNote: RAG Execute created one isolated test Knowledge collection on the live target; Rollback (verified idempotent on a repeated call) genuinely deleted the remote file and Knowledge collection, and the local test fixture was removed -- net state fully reverted, confirmed via pre/post remote file-existence and knowledge-collection checks. This is separate from the physical Greenfield installer run recorded under results.greenfieldAcceptance, which targeted a disposable Hyper-V VM, not the persistent real target machine referenced here. Separately, the 2.7.0 Codex Local LM Studio timing fix's live-target validation stopped and let the managed starter restart the real target's local LM Studio API server (GUI left running throughout) -- net state fully reverted (server reachable again, same as before); the starter-failure-path proof used a synthetic starter under a disposable scratch directory only, never the real production starter. For 2.8.0, the managed OpenWebUI update acceptance ran two real administrator-elevated Complete Installer Upgrade transactions against C:\KI-Stack with kernel-config.json temporarily retargeted to 0.10.2 and back to 0.11.0 (reverted exactly in the source repo afterward, byte-identical to the committed state), and genuinely downgraded then upgraded the real OpenWebUI venv package via Update-KIStack-OpenWebUI.ps1 -- net state fully reverted to the pinned 0.11.0, confirmed via direct venv version readback and a passing HTTP healthcheck. The pre-existing five accumulated stale/misplaced CutoverRuntime payload zips under installer/complete were also genuinely reduced to one by the payload-hygiene fix during these same real runs, which is the intended, permanent end state, not something reverted. For 2.9.0, the ReplayComponent acceptance ran a real, interactive, administrator-elevated Start-KIStackCompleteInstaller.ps1 -ReplayComponent openwebui-visual-pack transaction against the already-compliant real Visual Pack on C:\KI-Stack: this genuinely re-ran the existing Visual Pack install/validate path (real backup created, real API key entered interactively as a SecureString and never persisted, real browser-based first-login/API-key flow, real image and video generation tests both passing) and left the target functionally unchanged (same pinned Visual Pack version, same OpenWebUI/ComfyUI health, no second venv or other unexpected mutation) -- this is the intended, idempotent end state of a Replay, not something requiring reversion. For 2.10.0, the Update-KIStack-All acceptance was a single read-only -CheckOnly run against C:\KI-Stack: it queried the real installed/pinned state of every managed component plus a real PyPI upstream lookup for OpenWebUI, and performed no mutation whatsoever -- the real target's genuine drift (OpenWebUI already at 0.11.1 against the 0.11.0 pin) was observed and reported, not corrected, by design. For 2.12.0 (Cutover Runtime 1.6.14, Agent Pack 1.9.0 incl. the new ki-stack-research profile and the reconcile field-ownership/preserve fix, RAG 0.4.0 incl. project-scope separation), no real target was accessed or mutated: this cycle's validation is a source-only build plus mocked-HTTP regression coverage (see regressionSuites above) and the deterministic dual-build/PackageSelfTest evidence recorded elsewhere in this report; a real authenticated multi-step chat end-to-end proof for ki-stack-research remains blocked by the documented OpenWebUI admin-credential gap and was deliberately not worked around. For 2.13.0, the real target (C:\KI-Stack) was genuinely accessed and mutated across three independent workstreams, each fully reverted or left in its intended, permanent end state: (1) the OpenWebUI Credential Bootstrap was run interactively by the operator against the real, installed OpenWebUI 0.11.1 (ENABLE_API_KEYS enabled via the real admin-config API, a real persistent sk-... API key minted and stored DPAPI-encrypted locally, never in the repository), and then used to create one real 'KI-Stack Controlled Knowledge' collection read back via the real API as a genuine authenticated-access proof, with no foreign users or keys touched; (2) Codex Local was genuinely upgraded on the real target from 0.1.4 to 0.2.1 via Invoke-KIStackIsolatedComponentUpdate, followed by a real codex exec end-to-end call through the newly isolated CODEX_HOME, with the real, shared %USERPROFILE%\.codex confirmed byte-identical before and after via raw-text snapshot comparison; (3) the Research Agent web-search root-cause work created two temporary diagnostic OpenWebUI chats against the real instance (both deleted afterward, confirmed via a before/after chat-list comparison) and performed a real, manual SearXNG query plus a real fetch_url call to the public GitHub releases page as part of completing a genuine tool-calling round trip -- no other real chats, users, or configuration were altered. The four consolidation fixes (desktop-shortcut isolation, startup healthcheck retry, Codex status detection, WSL keeper review) were validated via isolated fixtures and structural checks only, except for the Codex status detection fix's realTargetValidation, which read (never mutated) the real target's live status.
